intro: You're looking for an auto enrolment advisor near you because your business has to set up a workplace pension that meets The Pensions Regulator's rules. Whether you're taking on your first member of staff or need help with an existing scheme, a local adviser can guide you through enrolling eligible staff and keeping on top of your duties. We introduce you to a suitable UK pension adviser who will quote you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What people searching for an auto enrolment advisor near me usually need
need_lead: Most employers looking for an auto enrolment advisor near me want practical help with the legal duties that come with running a workplace pension.
needs: You've just taken on your first employee and need to know whether auto enrolment applies to you and what to do first.
You already have a scheme but aren't sure if your payroll is set up correctly to enrol staff and process contributions.
You're unsure which staff count as eligible and want help assessing your workforce.
You need to complete a declaration of compliance with The Pensions Regulator and want to get it right.
You're concerned about keeping records and meeting ongoing duties such as re-enrolment and communicating with staff.
context_heading: What to understand about auto enrolment advice
context: Auto enrolment advice is a regulated activity, so any adviser you speak to should be authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) or be an appointed representative of an authorised firm. You can check this on the FCA register. If something goes wrong, you can complain to the firm and then to the Financial Ombudsman Service, and the Financial Services Compensation Scheme may protect you if an authorised firm fails.

Some pension decisions carry special rules: if you're considering transferring out of a defined benefit (final salary) scheme above a set value, the advice must come from an adviser with pension transfer specialist permissions. Safeguarded benefits also deserve particular care. Free, impartial guidance is available from Pension Wise for people over the age of fifty with defined contribution pensions.

faqs.q: Do I need an adviser to set up auto enrolment?
faqs.a: You can set up auto enrolment yourself, but many employers use an adviser to make sure they meet all their duties. An adviser can help you assess staff, choose a scheme and complete your declaration of compliance.

faqs.q: What does an auto enrolment adviser actually do?
faqs.a: They help employers set up compliant workplace pensions, assess staff and meet Pensions Regulator duties. This includes checking payroll integration and supporting you with declarations of compliance.

faqs.q: How do I check an adviser is properly authorised?
faqs.a: Financial advice in the UK is regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA). You can check the FCA register to see if an adviser or firm is authorised, or is an appointed representative of an authorised firm.

faqs.q: What if I'm unhappy with the advice I receive?
faqs.a: If something goes wrong, you can complain to the firm first. If you're not satisfied, you can then complain to the Financial Ombudsman Service, and the Financial Services Compensation Scheme may protect you if an authorised firm fails.

extra_heading: Choosing an adviser who deals with employers, not just pensions
extra: Your search for an auto enrolment advisor near me suggests you're an employer with duties to meet, not someone sorting out their own retirement pot. That distinction matters, because the help you need is about assessing staff, choosing a qualifying scheme and keeping the paperwork straight with The Pensions Regulator, rather than picking a fund for yourself. Look for someone who regularly works with employers on workplace pensions and is comfortable talking to whoever runs your payroll.

When you compare advisers, ask how they would handle the practical side: identifying eligible staff, working out when to enrol them, and making sure contributions flow correctly through your payroll. A useful conversation will cover your declaration of compliance and what happens at re-enrolment, so you understand the ongoing duties rather than just the initial setup. Fees are quoted on application, so ask each adviser to set out what they charge and exactly what that covers before you commit.

Meeting locally can make it easier to sit down with your payroll paperwork and staff details, but remote help works just as well if that suits you better. At a first appointment, expect questions about your workforce, your existing pension arrangements and any letters from The Pensions Regulator, so have those to hand. It's also worth checking the adviser or firm on the FCA register beforehand, since auto enrolment advice is a regulated activity.

extra_faqs.q: Is an auto enrolment adviser the same as a pension adviser for individuals?
extra_faqs.a: Not quite. An auto enrolment adviser helps you as an employer meet your workplace pension duties, such as assessing staff and completing declarations of compliance. A pension adviser for individuals focuses on your own retirement planning instead.

extra_faqs.q: Can my accountant or payroll bureau handle auto enrolment for me?
extra_faqs.a: Many employers rely on their payroll provider for the mechanics of processing contributions, but the legal duties remain yours as the employer. An adviser can work alongside your payroll to make sure the scheme and the payroll are joined up properly.

extra_faqs.q: What should I bring to a first meeting about auto enrolment?
extra_faqs.a: Bring details of your staff and their ages and earnings, any existing workplace pension arrangements, and any correspondence from The Pensions Regulator. That lets the adviser understand your position and explain what needs doing next.
